endpoint.note: upstream's target is the block output before the final norm; unembed supplies the norm, so it is not HF hidden_states[-1]

pair_weighting.note: equal per-prompt weighting makes the corpus length distribution part of the estimator; upstream's fit() weights the same way
pair_weighting.per_prompt: equal weight per prompt regardless of n_valid_positions
pair_weighting.source_target_pairs: causal, p' >= p, within the selected set

position_weighting.readout_warning: this lens was fitted at the max_seq_len recorded here; upstream's readout defaults (HFLensModel.encode and JacobianLens.apply, both 512) are larger than its fit default (128) and neither warns, so a readout beyond the fitted length is extrapolation and must be passed explicitly
position_weighting.scale_warning: J scales with the number of selected target positions, so fits at different max_seq_len or different band widths are not comparable in magnitude
position_weighting.target_reduction: sum over selected target positions, not normalised

precision.note: no autograd graph is built: this estimator differences forward passes, so the accumulation dtype describes the running sum rather than a backward pass

upstream.retired_when: this estimator exists to produce the golden comparison's second operand once; it is not a fitting path the programme keeps
